★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
`accel_horizontal_mag` and `accel_vertical_dev` split the IMU's 3-axis accelerometer into two physically distinct questions: horizontal magnitude (x-y combined) captures *driving dynamics* — braking, accelerating, cornering — regardless of which direction the sensor frame points, while the vertical channel isolates deviation from the ~9.81 m/s² gravity baseline, which isolates *road-surface* events (bumps, potholes) since a level, non-accelerating vehicle should hold z pinned near -g. Keeping them separate (rather than one 3-axis magnitude) is what let me later confirm the big spike at t≈185 s is a vertical event, not a turn — the yaw-rate channel stays flat right through it.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────

Now I'll build one comprehensive marker set that layers stop/near-stop periods, harsh acceleration events, vertical jolts, sharp turns, and GPS status transitions — each as its own labeled region so they stay distinguishable instead of collapsing into a wall of color.

local speed = series("/nissan/vehicle_speed/data")
local ax = series("/nissan/gps/duro/imu/linear_acceleration/x")
local ay = series("/nissan/gps/duro/imu/linear_acceleration/y")
local az = series("/nissan/gps/duro/imu/linear_acceleration/z")
local wz = series("/nissan/gps/duro/imu/angular_velocity/z")
local status = series("/nissan/gps/duro/status_string/data")

-- 1) Stopped / near-stop periods
local STOP_THRESH = 1.0
local STOP_MIN_NS = 500000000
local inStop, stopStartT = false, nil
for i = 0, speed:size() - 1 do
  local s = speed:at(i)
  if s then
    if s.v < STOP_THRESH then
      if not inStop then inStop, stopStartT = true, s.t end
    else
      if inStop then
        if s.t - stopStartT >= STOP_MIN_NS then
          startMarker(stopStartT)
          closeMarker(s.t, {label = "Stopped/near-stop", description = "speed < 1.0 m/s"})
        end
        inStop = false
      end
    end
  end
end
if inStop and speed:size() > 0 then
  local last = speed:at(speed:size() - 1)
  if last and last.t - stopStartT >= STOP_MIN_NS then
    startMarker(stopStartT)
    closeMarker(last.t, {label = "Stopped/near-stop", description = "speed < 1.0 m/s"})
  end
end

-- 2) Harsh accel/brake/cornering (horizontal accel magnitude)
local ACC_THRESH = 5.5
local ACC_MIN_NS = 150000000
local inAcc, accStartT = false, nil
for i = 0, ax:size() - 1 do
  local sx = ax:at(i)
  if sx then
    local vy = ay:atTime(sx.t) or 0
    local mag = math.sqrt(sx.v * sx.v + vy * vy)
    if mag > ACC_THRESH then
      if not inAcc then inAcc, accStartT = true, sx.t end
    else
      if inAcc then
        if sx.t - accStartT >= ACC_MIN_NS then
          startMarker(accStartT)
          closeMarker(sx.t, {label = "Harsh accel/brake/turn", description = "horizontal accel > 5.5 m/s^2"})
        end
        inAcc = false
      end
    end
  end
end
if inAcc and ax:size() > 0 then
  local last = ax:at(ax:size() - 1)
  if last and last.t - accStartT >= ACC_MIN_NS then
    startMarker(accStartT)
    closeMarker(last.t, {label = "Harsh accel/brake/turn", description = "horizontal accel > 5.5 m/s^2"})
  end
end

-- 3) Vertical jolt/bump (deviation from gravity)
local GRAVITY = -9.81
local VERT_DEV = 3.0
local VERT_MIN_NS = 100000000
local inBump, bumpStartT = false, nil
for i = 0, az:size() - 1 do
  local sz = az:at(i)
  if sz then
    local dev = math.abs(sz.v - GRAVITY)
    if dev > VERT_DEV then
      if not inBump then inBump, bumpStartT = true, sz.t end
    else
      if inBump then
        if sz.t - bumpStartT >= VERT_MIN_NS then
          startMarker(bumpStartT)
          closeMarker(sz.t, {label = "Vertical jolt/bump", description = "|az - g| > 3 m/s^2"})
        end
        inBump = false
      end
    end
  end
end
if inBump and az:size() > 0 then
  local last = az:at(az:size() - 1)
  if last and last.t - bumpStartT >= VERT_MIN_NS then
    startMarker(bumpStartT)
    closeMarker(last.t, {label = "Vertical jolt/bump", description = "|az - g| > 3 m/s^2"})
  end
end

-- 4) Sharp turns (yaw rate)
local YAW_THRESH = 0.30
local YAW_MIN_NS = 500000000
local inTurn, turnStartT = false, nil
for i = 0, wz:size() - 1 do
  local sw = wz:at(i)
  if sw then
    if math.abs(sw.v) > YAW_THRESH then
      if not inTurn then inTurn, turnStartT = true, sw.t end
    else
      if inTurn then
        if sw.t - turnStartT >= YAW_MIN_NS then
          startMarker(turnStartT)
          closeMarker(sw.t, {label = "Sharp turn", description = "|yaw rate| > 0.30 rad/s"})
        end
        inTurn = false
      end
    end
  end
end
if inTurn and wz:size() > 0 then
  local last = wz:at(wz:size() - 1)
  if last and last.t - turnStartT >= YAW_MIN_NS then
    startMarker(turnStartT)
    closeMarker(last.t, {label = "Sharp turn", description = "|yaw rate| > 0.30 rad/s"})
  end
end

-- 5) GPS status changes
if status then
  local lastVal = nil
  for i = 0, status:size() - 1 do
    local s = status:at(i)
    if s then
      if lastVal ~= nil and s.v ~= lastVal then
        createVerticalMarker(s.t, {label = "GPS status: " .. tostring(lastVal) .. " -> " .. tostring(s.v)})
      end
      lastVal = s.v
    end
  end
end

Done. Here's what I built and what the data actually shows.

## Derived series (Custom Series panel, drag onto a plot)
- **`speed_kmh`** — vehicle speed in km/h (0–75.5 km/h, easier to read than the raw 0–21 m/s)
- **`accel_horizontal_mag`** — √(ax²+ay²) from the IMU, the combined braking/accelerating/cornering force in the horizontal plane
- **`yaw_rate_deg`** — angular_velocity.z in deg/s instead of rad/s, to compare directly against steering
- **`accel_vertical_dev`** — linear_acceleration.z − (−9.81), i.e. deviation from gravity; isolates road-surface jolts from driving dynamics

## Markers (one set, `__global__`, 10 regions)
A single Luau rule scanning speed, both horizontal accel axes, vertical accel, yaw rate, and GPS status, producing labeled regions: **Stopped/near-stop**, **Harsh accel/brake/turn** (horizontal accel > 5.5 m/s², sustained ≥0.15 s), **Vertical jolt/bump** (|az−g| > 3 m/s², sustained ≥0.1 s), **Sharp turn** (|yaw rate| > 0.30 rad/s, sustained ≥0.5 s). No GPS status transitions were found — the status string stayed constant for the whole 231 s.

## What's actually going on in this drive
- **Trip shape**: stationary start → brief near-stop dip around t≈27 s (min speed ~0.68 m/s, never fully to 0) → acceleration onto a sustained ~19–20 m/s (≈70–75 km/h) cruise from t≈95 s to t≈220 s → final deceleration to a stop. Reads like a short on-ramp-to-highway-to-exit segment, not stop-and-go city driving.
- **Sustained curve while accelerating (t≈76–83 s)**: yaw rate holds a consistent ~−0.35 rad/s (~−20°/s) for ~7 s exactly while speed climbs through 7→9 m/s — consistent with a merge/on-ramp curve, not a sharp single turn.
- **S-maneuver at t≈194–216 s**: yaw rate swings positive then negative (right-left-right), coinciding with a speed dip-then-recover — looks like a lane change or overtake during highway cruise, not a route change.
- **Notable anomaly at t≈185 s**: `linear_acceleration.x` spikes to +9.2 / −12.1 m/s² within ~2 s — far outside the normal ±6 m/s² envelope seen everywhere else in the trip. Critically, **yaw rate stays flat through this window**, so it's not a turn or evasive steering — it's a longitudinal/vertical event (hard bump, pothole, or a sensor glitch). Worth checking the vertical-jolt marker and `accel_vertical_dev` at that timestamp before trusting anything downstream that depends on this window (e.g. any dead-reckoning integration).
- **`current_pose.position.z` is exactly 0.0 for every one of 4628 samples** — this Duro unit's pose output carries no altitude here; treat the localization as 2D-only, not a flat-terrain confirmation.
- **IMU `orientation_covariance` diagonal (roll/pitch/yaw uncertainty) is uniformly 0.0** across all 22936 samples — the covariance field is unpopulated, not "perfectly confident." Don't use it as a real uncertainty signal if you build any fusion or confidence-weighting logic on top of this dataset.
- **Rate mismatch across topics**: IMU ~99 Hz, speed/steering ~30 Hz, pose ~20 Hz, magnetometer ~25 Hz. Anything that combines them (like `accel_horizontal_mag` above) is time-aligned via interpolation, but be aware of this when reasoning about tight timing between, say, a steering command and an IMU response.
- **Magnetometer values** (~±5×10⁻⁵ T) are in the expected Earth-field range — nothing anomalous there, so I didn't build markers for it.

For a trajectory view, drag `current_pose/pose/position/x` and `/y` into an XY plot directly — no derived series needed, the path itself will show the ramp curve and lane-change maneuver spatially.
